question: What is cervicitis?
explanation: Cervicitis refers specifically to the inflammation of the mucosal and epithelial tissues of the cervix. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T14#GNS216_U5_T14_h1)

question: How does chronic cervicitis mainly differ from acute cervicitis?

options.A: It involves long-standing immune cell changes in the tissue.
options.B: It presents with sudden, severe pus-like discharge.
options.C: It never requires any medical or nursing intervention.
options.D: It is always caused by viral agents rather than bacteria.

explanation: Think of acute as sudden and angry with quick pus, while chronic is a longer-lasting, low-grade immune response in the tissue.

question: Which common bacterium that lives inside cells is frequently responsible for cervicitis?
explanation: Chlamydia trachomatis is a well-known bug that loves to hide inside cervical cells and cause inflammation.

question: What is a common non-infectious cause of cervical inflammation?

options.A: Increased dietary intake of refined sugars
options.C: Normal fluctuations in monthly estrogen levels

explanation: Not all inflammation comes from germs! Things like chemical spermicides or barrier devices can irritate the delicate cervical tissue.

question: What is the name of the vulnerable zone where columnar and squamous epithelium meet on the cervix?
explanation: The transformation zone is the specific anatomical junction where different types of cervical cells meet, making it highly susceptible to infections and inflammation. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T14#GNS216_U5_T14_h3)

question: Why does an inflamed cervix tend to bleed easily during an examination?

options.A: Complete destruction of the underlying muscle layer
options.B: Fragile tissues and tiny blood vessels opening up from inflammation
options.C: Rapid overproduction of red blood cells by the cervix
options.D: Severe blood clotting disorders throughout the body

explanation: When tissue is inflamed, blood rushes to the area and the vessels become delicate, meaning even a gentle touch can cause spotting.

question: Which symptom is a classic presentation of cervical friability in cervicitis?
explanation: Because inflamed cervical tissue is very fragile, contact during sexual intercourse frequently causes postcoital spotting or bleeding. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T14#GNS216_U5_T14_h4)

question: A female client reports a thick vaginal discharge and spotting after intercourse. Which condition should you suspect first as a nurse?
explanation: Unusual discharge paired with bleeding after sex are classic clues pointing right to cervical inflammation.

question: What is the best and most accurate lab test used to confirm chlamydia and gonorrhea infections of the cervix?
explanation: NAAT is the gold-standard test because it is super sensitive at picking up bacterial DNA from a simple swab or urine sample.

question: What key visual finding does a clinician look for on the cervix during a speculum exam for acute cervicitis?

options.A: Pus-like discharge and tissue that bleeds easily
options.B: Complete closure of the internal cervical opening
options.C: Large fluid-filled cysts across the surface
options.D: Pale, dry, and glistening epithelial layers

explanation: During an exam, an angry, infected cervix often shows pus draining out and tissue that is fragile and bleeds at a touch.

question: Why are antibiotics often started right away before lab results are even back?

options.A: To reduce the financial cost of laboratory diagnostic supplies
options.B: To completely eliminate the need for any follow-up testing
options.C: To cure viral infections like herpes simplex immediately
options.D: To stop the infection from spreading upward into the reproductive tract

explanation: Starting treatment fast prevents the infection from traveling up into the uterus and fallopian tubes, avoiding bigger problems later.

question: What essential instruction must be given about sexual partners when treating infectious cervicitis?

options.A: Partners can continue unprotected intercourse during the treatment week.
options.B: Partners only need treatment if they develop severe abdominal pain.
options.C: Only partners with visible symptoms need prescription medication.
options.D: Sexual partners must be checked and treated at the same time.

explanation: Treating partners together is the only way to stop the annoying ping-pong game of passing the infection back and forth!

question: What major upper reproductive tract condition can happen if cervicitis is left untreated?
explanation: If lower tract infections aren't cleared, they can creep upward and turn into pelvic inflammatory disease (PID).

question: How does untreated cervicitis affect a patient's risk of contracting HIV?

options.A: It grants temporary immunity against sexually transmitted viruses.
options.B: It decreases the risk because white blood cells destroy the virus.
options.C: It increases the risk because the mucosal tissue is broken and immune cells are rushed to the area.
options.D: It has no measurable impact on viral transmission rates.

explanation: Inflamed, fragile tissue plus a gathering of immune cells gives viruses like HIV an easier pathway into the body.

question: What is the most important piece of advice to give a patient taking a 7-day course of antibiotics for cervicitis?

options.A: Share the remaining pills with your partner to save money.
options.B: Double the next dose if you forget to take one pill.
options.C: Stop taking the pills immediately if mild stomach upset occurs.
options.D: Finish all the medication even if you start feeling better early.

explanation: Always remind patients to complete their full dose! Stopping early can cause the infection to bounce back stronger.

question: Which of these is NOT something a nurse should tell a patient being treated for infectious cervicitis?

options.A: Use barrier methods consistently to help prevent reinfection.
options.B: Make sure your sexual partner is treated at the same time.
options.C: Stop taking your medicine as soon as the discharge lessens.
options.D: Avoid having sex until your treatment is fully completed.

explanation: Never advise stopping meds early just because symptoms fade. They must finish the entire course!
